searchText: how can you compute the entry queue validators count? I was thinking of doing `deposit_count - last validator_index (+1)` but it gives a value different from https://www.validatorqueue.com/ It's the list of validators that have `activation_epoch > current_epoch`. Currently you just need to find out the smallest index that satisfies this condition, and just take the length of the validator set minus that index. if you do deposit count you will be counting validators that haven't been voted yet in the beacon chain, you would also be counting partial deposits as new validators, etc. how can I compute the estimated time taken for a validator to go from depositing 32 eth on DepositContract to validator getting activated on beacon chain? I’m think we could do it this way: eth1_follow_distance delay + eth1_data voting round + (DepositContract.deposit_count - block.body.eth1_data.deposit_count) / MAX_DEPOSIT + pending_validators / churn_limit. but it also counts partial deposits, so not accurate. this is not possible to compute accurately today since it would depend on the eth1 voting period and ultimately on the dynamics of how clients implement their eth1 voting algorithm (some used to follow the majority, others imposed certain conditions) you are counting a full eth1 data voting round but it may be less depending on when the deposit was included. if you want add rollup-centric to Ethereum with this protocol proto-dank-sharding so you should or you can give a rollup project repository(client node ) to rollup operators run it so anyone can run and be a rulluper🥸 Please an informed expert answer

excerpts.content: It's the list of validators that have `activation_epoch > current_epoch`. Currently you just need to find out the smallest index that satisfies this condition, and just take the length of the validator set minus that index.
